It was assumed that the coal gasification facility would be located in Sarpy Creek Valley south of the current Westmoreland Resources administration building. Here the surrounding terrain is approximately 100 meters higher than plant grade and the terrain will thus have adverse effects on resultant ground level concentrations from stack released emissions. The possibility of the effluent plume intersecting the Little Wolf Mountains, which are located about 10 miles (16 kilometers) east of the plant site and rise approximately 400 meters above plant grade, must be considered.
Maximum long-term and short-term ground level concentrations resulting from the stack emissions from the gasification facility and the accompanying power generating facility were calculated and compared to the Montana and Federal air quality standards presented in Table III-13, III-14, and III-15.
